messages.content: Can you tell me a story where a brave red bird protects its family from red spiders and is thanked by its friends with an invitation to a special party in the sky?

Once upon a time there was a big red bird. The bird was very brave, and it liked to protect its family. Every day it invited its friends to join it in the sky and they would play together.
One day they saw something new in the sky. It was very big and red, and they had to be careful. The red bird stayed near to protect its family.
Suddenly the red bird saw red spiders! It was scared, but it knew it had to protect its family. So the red bird used its wings and its beak to scare away the spiders.
The other birds were so thankful! They all said thank you to the brave red bird, and gave it an invitation to a special party in the sky.
The red bird said yes, of course! It was so happy to be able to protect its family, and it was excited for the party.
The end.
You are a storyteller for young children. In your stories, the characters talk to each other.

Can you tell me a story where Jen and Tom are sad because it's raining and they can't go on holiday with their parents, but the next day they see a rainbow and their parents surprise them with a trip to the beach?

Jen and Tom were sad. They wanted to go on holiday with Mom and Dad, but it was gray and rainy outside. They could not play in the park or swim in the pool. They had to stay in the house and watch TV.
"Can we go on holiday tomorrow?" Jen asked Mom.
Mom shook her head. "No, honey, we have to wait until the rain stops. Maybe next week."
Jen and Tom sighed. They hoped the rain would stop soon. They wanted to see the sun and the sea and the sand. They wanted to have fun and make new friends.
The next day, they woke up and looked out the window. They saw a big rainbow in the sky. The rain was gone and the sun was shining.
"Look, look!" Tom shouted. "It's a rainbow! That means good luck!"
Mom and Dad came into their room. They smiled and hugged them.
"Guess what?" Dad said. "We have a surprise for you. We are going on holiday today! We have packed our bags and we have tickets for the train. We are going to the beach!"
Jen and Tom jumped up and down. They were so happy. They thanked Mom and Dad and ran to get ready.
They hoped the holiday would be the best ever. They could not wait to see the beach. They hoped they would find shells and starfish and crabs. They hoped they would have a lot of fun.

Write a short story in which Tom and Sue couldn't agree on which yogurt to buy, so their mom let them each pick one. They ended up picking the same kind by mistake, which tasted just like a disgusting yogurt they had tried before. They laughed and learned to check the flavor before buying yogurt.

One day, Tom and Sue went to the store with their mom. They wanted to buy some yogurt. Tom liked the red yogurt, but Sue liked the green yogurt. They could not agree on which one to get, so their mom said they could each pick one.
On the way home, Tom said, "Sue, I remember when we tried that disgusting yogurt at Grandma's house. It was so bad!" Sue laughed and said, "I remember that too, Tom! It was so yucky!" They both laughed and could not wait to eat their new yogurt when they got home.
When they got home, they opened their yogurt and started to eat. Suddenly, they both made a funny face. Their yogurt tasted just like the disgusting yogurt from Grandma's house! They looked at each other and laughed. They had picked the same kind of yogurt by mistake! From then on, they always checked the flavor before buying yogurt.

You are a storyteller for young children. In your stories, the characters talk to each other. Your stories have a problem that the characters must solve.
Write a short story in which Timmy and his friends plan a picnic in the park, but encounter ants. Timmy reassures his friend Sarah that the ants are harmless and they all have a great time.

Once upon a time, there was a little boy named Timmy. Timmy loved to play outside with his friends. One day, Timmy and his friends wanted to have a picnic in the park. They planned to bring sandwiches, fruit, and juice.
Timmy's mom gave him a notebook to write down what they needed for the picnic. Timmy wrote down everything they needed in his notebook. He was very excited for the picnic.
When they arrived at the park, they found out that there were ants everywhere! Timmy's friend, Sarah, was scared of the ants because she thought they were harmful. Timmy told her that the ants were harmless and that they just wanted to eat the crumbs from their sandwiches.
Sarah felt better and they all had a great time at the picnic. Timmy was happy that he planned everything in his notebook and that they were able to enjoy the day without any problems.
Now tell me a story where an old house with cracked walls and chipped paint was restored to its former beauty by an honest painter who worked hard and painted the walls with bright colors.

Once upon a time, there was a house. It was very old and needed some help. The walls were cracked and the paint was chipped. The people who lived in the house wanted to make it pretty again. They called a painter to help them. The painter was very honest and said he could restore the house to its former beauty. He worked very hard and painted the walls with bright colors. When he was finished, the house looked brand new! Everyone was very happy and thanked the painter for his hard work.
You are a storyteller for young children.

I would like a story where Tommy goes to the park with his mom and meets a jolly old man who gives him a hug when he feels sad. Tommy forgets to say thank you, but his mom tells him it's never too late and he goes back to thank the man.

Once upon a time, there was a little boy named Tommy. Tommy loved to play with his toys and run around outside. One day, Tommy went to the park with his mom. He was so excited to go down the slide and swing on the swings. 
While they were playing, Tommy's mom got a phone call and had to leave the park for a little while. Tommy felt sad and started to cry. But then, a jolly old man came over and gave him a big hug. Tommy felt better and started to play again. 
After a while, Tommy's mom came back to the park. She asked him if he had a good time and Tommy said yes. But then he realized that he forgot to say thank you to the jolly old man who gave him a hug. Tommy felt bad, but his mom told him it's never too late to say thank you. So, Tommy ran back to the jolly old man and said thank you for the hug. The jolly old man smiled and Tommy felt happy again.

Can you tell me a story where Lily loses the key to her toy box and her friend Timmy helps her open it with a paper clip?

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Lily. She had a special box with a lock on it to keep her toys safe. One day, Lily lost the key to her box and couldn't open it. She was sad and asked her friend, Timmy, for help.
Timmy asked, "What's wrong, Lily?"
"I can't open my box because I lost the key," Lily replied.
"Don't worry, I can help you," Timmy said. He used a paper clip to part the lock and open the box. Lily was glad and gave Timmy a big hug. 
"Thank you, Timmy! You're the best friend ever," Lily said with a smile. From that day on, Lily kept her key in a safe place so she wouldn't lose it again.

I would like a story where a cat and a dog become friends after the dog helps the cat retrieve a ball that had rolled under a chair.

Once there was a cat with soft fur. The cat liked to play with a ball. One day, the ball went under a big chair. The cat tried to get the ball, but she could not reach it.
A dog saw the cat and came to help. The dog was big and strong. He put his head under the chair and got the ball for the cat. The cat was very grateful.
The cat said thank you to the dog. She bowed her head to show she was happy. The dog and the cat became good friends. They played with the ball together every day.
You are a storyteller for young children. In your stories, the characters talk to each other.
Tell me a story in which Lily and Ben make soup from grass and dirt in the backyard and a friendly truck comes by and gives them toys in exchange for sharing their soup.

Lily and Ben are playing in the backyard. They have a big truck and a small pot. They pretend to cook soup with grass and dirt.
"Yum, yum, soup is ready!" Lily says. She puts some soup in a cup and gives it to Ben.
"Thank you, Lily!" Ben says. He pretends to sip the soup. "This is the best soup ever!"
They hear a loud honk. They look up and see a big yellow truck on the street. It has a funny face and a long nose.
"Wow, look at that truck!" Ben says. He runs to the fence to see it better.
"Hi, truck!" Lily says. She waves to the truck.
The truck honks again and winks at them. It has a silly voice.
"Hello, kids!" the truck says. "Do you want to see what I have in my back?"
"Yes, please!" Lily and Ben say.
The truck opens its back and shows them a lot of toys. There are dolls, cars, balls, books, and more.
"Wow, so many toys!" Lily says.
"These are for you!" the truck says. "You can have one each. But you have to do something for me first."
"What do we have to do?" Ben asks.
"You have to share your soup with me!" the truck says. "I'm very hungry and your soup smells delicious!"
Lily and Ben laugh. They think the truck is very silly. They bring their pot and cups to the truck.
"Here you go, truck!" Lily says. She pours some soup in a big bowl and gives it to the truck.
"Thank you, Lily!" the truck says. He pretends to slurp the soup. "This is the best soup ever!"
Lily and Ben smile. They are happy to share their soup with the truck. They pick their toys and thank the truck.
"Bye, truck!" they say.
"Bye, kids!" the truck says. He honks and drives away.
Lily and Ben hug their toys. They go back to their backyard and play some more. They have a lot of fun.

Write a short story in which two best friends, Sam and Jenny, go on a fun trip to the airport where Jenny overcomes her nervousness and they watch an airplane take off on their adventure.

Once upon a time, there were two best friends: Sam and Jenny. Sam suggested that they take a fun trip to the airport. Jenny thought this was a great idea and was so excited.
As they arrived at the airport, Jenny became a bit nervous. She had never been to an airport before. Sam thought she didn't need to feel scared and said, "Don't be so nervous, it'll be fun!"
The two went through security together, and as they did, Sam told Jenny about all the fun things they could do and the special airplanes they would see. Jenny was getting more excited by the minute.
When they got to the gate, Sam suggested that they take their seats and wait for the airplane to arrive. Jenny gave Sam a big hug before they sat down.
Soon, the airplane came and they watched it land. Jenny was so excited that she completely forgot she was nervous! Together they watched the airplane taxi to the gate, and before they knew it they were saying goodbye as they took off on their adventure.
Write a story that uses the words try, dish, and sweet.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Lily. She wanted to make a sweet dish for her mommy's birthday. She went to the kitchen and tried to find a recipe. She found one for chocolate cake and tried to make it.
Lily put all the ingredients in a bowl and mixed them together. She tried to make sure everything was mixed well. Then, she put the mixture in a dish and put it in the oven. She tried to be patient while it baked.
Finally, the cake was done and it smelled sweet. Lily took it out of the oven and put it on the table. She tried to decorate it with frosting and candles. When her mommy saw the cake, she was so happy and said it was the sweetest dish she had ever tasted. Lily was very proud and happy that she tried to make her mommy's birthday special.
You are a storyteller for young children. In your stories, the characters talk to each other.
Tell me a story in which Timmy shares a branch from his apple tree with his friend Billy, so that Billy can have his own apple tree. They become great friends and share their apples.

Once upon a time, there was a little boy named Timmy. Timmy had a big apple tree in his backyard. He loved to climb it and eat the juicy apples. One day, Timmy's friend Billy came over to play. 
"Wow, Timmy, your apple tree is so big!" said Billy. 
"Yes, and it gives me lots of apples to eat," replied Timmy. 
"I wish I could gain a tree like this in my yard," said Billy. 
Timmy thought for a moment and then said, "You can cut a small branch from my tree and plant it in your yard. Then you will have your own apple tree!" 
"That's a great idea, Timmy! You are so honest," said Billy. 
Timmy smiled and they both climbed the tree to cut a branch. They planted it in Billy's yard and soon he had his own apple tree. From that day on, they shared their apples and had fun playing together.
Now tell me a story where a big pink elephant asked a small rabbit if he could sit on him, but the rabbit died under the elephant's weight, leaving the elephant feeling sad and alone.

Once upon a time, a big pink elephant was walking in the forest. He was very huge and everyone was afraid of him. The elephant wanted to sit down and rest, but he couldn't find a good spot. 
Suddenly, he saw a small rabbit hopping nearby. The elephant asked the rabbit, "Can I sit on you?" The rabbit said yes and the elephant sat on the rabbit's back. 
But the elephant was too heavy for the rabbit and he couldn't breathe. The rabbit tried to escape, but he couldn't move. Sadly, the rabbit died and the elephant was left alone in the forest. 
From that day on, the pink elephant realized that he should never sit on anyone again. He walked away from the forest, feeling very sad.
You are a storyteller for young children. In your stories, the characters talk to each other. Your stories have a sad ending.
Tell me a story with the words talk, powder, and clumsy.

One day, a clumsy boy named Tom went to the park. He saw his friend, Sue, and they started to talk. They talked about their toys and the fun games they played. Tom had a bag of powder with him that he found at home. He thought it was magic powder and wanted to show Sue.
"Look, Sue," said Tom. "I have magic powder!" Sue was excited to see the powder. Tom opened the bag and tried to make something magical happen. But he was so clumsy that he spilled the powder all over the ground.
"Oh no!" cried Sue. "The magic powder is gone!" Tom felt sad that he was so clumsy and lost the magic powder. Sue was sad too, and they both went home with heavy hearts. The day ended badly for both Tom and Sue, and they wished they had been more careful with the magic powder.
Tell me another story, in which Sue and her friends help a sad bug by fixing a hole in the soil, learning the value of teamwork.

One day, a little girl named Sue was playing in her yard. She saw a big hole in the soil. Sue was confused. She did not know who made the hole. She wanted to solve the problem.
Sue asked her friends, Tom and Lily, to help her. They all looked at the hole. They saw a small bug. The bug was sad. It lost its home. Sue, Tom, and Lily wanted to help the bug.
They worked together to fix the hole for the bug. The bug was happy. Sue, Tom, and Lily were happy too. They learned that when they work together, they can solve any problem.
You are a storyteller for young children.
I would like a story where a little girl named Jane learns the importance of keeping her face clean and protecting her skin with the help of her mommy.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl. She was three years old and her name was Jane. Jane knew that it was very important to be healthy and keep her face clean.
Every morning, Jane's mommy would wash her face with warm water and clean it with a soft cloth. Then her mommy would put cream on Jane's skin to protect it.
"I protect my face, mommy," said Jane.
"That's right, Jane," said her mommy. "It's very important to protect your skin. That way, you will stay healthy and beautiful."
Jane was very happy. She liked that her mommy was taking care of her and protecting her skin. Jane smiled and said, "I love you, mommy!"
You are a storyteller for young children.

Can you tell me a story where Tim meets a new friend named Tom who is sometimes selfish and doesn't want to share his toys. Tom promises to share his toys if Tim takes a nap, and when Tim wakes up, Tom keeps his promise, and they become the best of friends?

Once upon a time, there was a little boy named Tim. He liked to play all day long. One day, Tim met a new friend named Tom. They liked to play together. But sometimes, Tom was selfish and did not want to share his toys.
One day, Tim's mom told him to take a nap. Tim did not want to nap. He wanted to play with Tom. Tom said, "If you nap, I promise to share my toys when you wake up." Tim thought about it and agreed to nap.
Tim took a short nap and woke up feeling happy. When he went to play with Tom, Tom kept his promise and shared his toys. They played together and had lots of fun. From that day on, Tom was not selfish anymore, and they became the best of friends.
You are a storyteller for young children. In your stories, the characters talk to each other. Your stories hint early at what will happen later.
I would like a story where Mia goes to the park with her mom and plays on the swings, and after playing, her mom gives her juice which makes her happy.

One day, a little girl named Mia went to the park with her mom. Mia was very happy because her mom allowed her to play on the swings. The sun was shining and the sky was clear.
Mia's mom said, "Mia, after you play, we can have some juice." Mia liked juice a lot. She played on the swings and the slide, and then she got thirsty. She remembered what her mom said about the juice.
Mia ran to her mom and said, "Mom, can I have the juice now?" Her mom smiled and gave her a cup of juice. Mia drank it all and felt very happy. The juice was so good, and the day was so fun.
Now tell me a story where a friendly dog named Max learns to listen to his owner and not go near fireworks after getting scared by one.

Once upon a time, there was a friendly dog named Max. Max loved to play with his ball and run around in the park. One day, Max was playing with his ball when he saw a firework in the sky. The firework was so pretty and colorful that Max wanted to see it up close.
Max ran towards the firework and suddenly, it exploded with a loud scream! Max got scared and ran back to his owner, who was sitting on a bench. Max's owner said, "I told you not to go near the fireworks, Max. They can be dangerous."
Max felt bad and realized that he should listen to his owner. From that day on, Max never went near the fireworks again. He learned that it's important to listen to the people who care about you and keep you safe.
You are a storyteller for young children.
I would like a story where Tim finds an envelope and asks his sister if he can study it. He learns the importance of being polite and discovers a pretty picture inside.

Once upon a time, in a small house, a little boy named Tim found an envelope. He did not know what was inside. He wanted to study it. Tim asked his mom, "Mom, can I open the envelope?" His mom said, "Yes, but be polite and ask your sister if it is hers."
Tim went to his sister and said, "Sis, is this your envelope? Can I study it?" His sister was happy that Tim asked politely. She said, "No, it is not mine. You can study it."
Tim opened the envelope and found a pretty picture. He showed it to his mom and sister. They all liked the picture. Tim learned that it is good to be polite and ask before doing something. They all lived happily ever after.
You are a storyteller for young children. In your stories, the characters talk to each other.
Tell me a story with the words wake, cart, and busy.

Sara and Ben are twins. They like to play with their cart. Their cart has four wheels and a big box. They can put toys, books, and snacks in the box. They can pull the cart with a rope.
One morning, Sara and Ben wake up early. They want to play with their cart. They put on their clothes and go to the living room. They see their cart by the sofa. They are happy.
"Let's go outside and play with our cart!" Sara says.
"OK, but we have to be quiet. Mom and Dad are still sleeping," Ben says.
They take their cart and go to the backyard. They see many birds, flowers, and bugs. They are busy. They fill their cart with leaves, rocks, and pine cones. They make a pile in the corner. They pretend they are building a house.
They have fun with their cart. They laugh and sing. They do not hear Mom and Dad coming outside.
"Good morning, Sara and Ben! You are up early!" Mom says.
"Hi, Mom! Hi, Dad! We are playing with our cart!" Sara says.
"We see that. You have a lot of things in your cart. What are you making?" Dad says.
"We are making a house for the birds and the bugs. Do you want to help us?" Ben says.
"Sure, we would love to help you. But first, how about some breakfast? You must be hungry after working so hard," Mom says.
"OK, we are hungry. Can we bring our cart inside?" Sara says.
"Of course, you can. But let's clean it up a bit first. We don't want to make a mess in the kitchen," Dad says.
They clean their cart and bring it inside. They have breakfast with Mom and Dad. They tell them about their cart and their house. Mom and Dad are proud of them. They hug them and kiss them.
They finish their breakfast and go back to the backyard. They continue to play with their cart and their house. They have a busy and happy day.

Now tell me a story where Sara and Ben try to catch a frog in the park, but it jumps away from them. They follow it and ask to be friends, but the frog is scared until they show kindness and respect. They become friends for a little while.

Sara and Ben are playing in the park. They see a little frog on the grass. The frog is green and has big eyes.
"Look, a frog!" Sara says. "Can we catch it?"
Ben nods. He likes frogs. He tries to grab the frog, but the frog is too fast. It jumps away from Ben's hand.
"Wow, it can jump very high!" Ben says. "Let's follow it!"
Sara and Ben run after the frog. The frog jumps from the grass to a rock, then to a flower, then to a tree. Sara and Ben try to keep up, but they are not as good at jumping as the frog.
"Wait for us, frog!" Sara calls. "We want to be your friends!"
The frog stops on a branch. It looks at Sara and Ben. It croaks.
"Ribbit, ribbit," the frog says. "You are too big to be my friends. You scare me. Go away!"
Sara and Ben feel sad. They do not want to scare the frog. They want to play with it.
"Please, frog, don't be afraid," Ben says. "We are nice. We won't hurt you. We just want to see you."
The frog thinks for a moment. It sees that Sara and Ben have kind faces and gentle voices. It decides to give them a chance.
"OK, OK," the frog says. "You can see me, but only for a little inch. Then you have to leave me alone. Deal?"
Sara and Ben smile. They agree to the deal. They come closer to the tree, but not too close. They look at the frog with wonder. The frog looks at them with curiosity.
They see how beautiful the frog is, with its shiny skin and bright colors. They hear how funny the frog sounds, with its croaky voice and loud noises. They learn how amazing the frog is, with its long legs and sticky tongue.
They are happy. The frog is happy. They are friends for a little inch.
You are a storyteller for young children.
Can you tell me a story where an alligator goes on an adventure to find excitement but feels disappointed until a frog shows him a grand and magical place full of wonders?

Once upon a time, there was a little alligator who lived in a pond. One day he decided to go on an adventure. So he hurried off, over the hills and far away.
As he traveled, he noticed many things. He saw flowers and tall grass. He saw a bee buzzing around. He even saw a bright rainbow in the sky. 
But the alligator felt that something was missing. Everything he saw was very dull and boring. He longed for something exciting. 
“I want an adventure!” he said, “Where can I find excitement?”
He looked around and couldn’t find anything. Feeling disappointed, he started to head back home. Then all of a sudden, he heard a voice.
“Wait,” said the voice, ”I can help you. Hurry, over here.” 
The alligator ran over to the voice. It was a frog, hopping around. The frog said, “Follow me! I know a grand place, full of fun and adventure.”
The alligator followed the frog and before long, he arrived at a grand and magical place full of wonders. He was so excited and delighted!
The alligator cheered and thanked the frog. He hurried around, exploring everything he saw. He had found his adventure, and he would never forget it.
You are a storyteller for young children. Your stories teach a lesson.
Can you tell me a story where a family learns to have fun in the rain by playing with their toys in the garden and learns the importance of balancing work and play?

Once upon a time there was a family who lived in a village near the woods. Every day, the family would go for walks in the woods to collect toys and play games.
One day, it started to rain. The family was sad, as they had hoped to spend the day outdoors. The dad told the family that even rain doesn't have to ruin their fun. He suggested they find a way to play with the toys in the rain.
The family used the rain to their advantage and they played with the toys in their garden. The toys got soaked, but everyone was happy and enjoyed their time.
At the end of the day, the dad reminded the family that serious work always should come first and play can come afterward. He said that when serious work is done, it is ok to make time for fun. The family agreed, and they all had a good night's sleep. 
The family learned an important lesson that day that rain can be fun when used the right way.
Write a short story in which a wise deer makes a new friend in the form of a little girl who he shares a moment with in the forest.

Once upon a time in a forest there was a wise deer. He wandered around the forest and enjoyed the sun on his fur. 
One day he was gazing around the forest when suddenly he noticed something. Someone else was gazing at him. It was a little 3 year old girl. She had big brown eyes that were staring directly at the deer. 
The wise deer felt comfortable, like he had known the little girl for a long time. He smiled and walked closer to her. She was very excited and smiled back at the deer. 
The two of them continued to gaze at one another for what felt like forever. The wise deer was happy that he had made a new friend. 
The girl then waved goodbye to the deer, who waved back at her. The deer watched as the girl skipped away, and then lay down in the sunshine and dreamed of meeting his new friend again.
You are a storyteller for young children. Your stories have a surprising twist.
Tell me a story with the words know, luxury, and enormous.

Once upon a time, there was a big, big cat. The cat lived in an enormous house. This house was very nice. The cat had many toys and good food. The cat did not know that this was called luxury.
One day, the cat saw a little mouse. The mouse was very small. The cat thought, "I will catch the mouse." The cat ran and ran, but the mouse was too fast. The cat was sad. The cat did not know that the mouse was special.
Then, one day, the cat and the mouse talked. The mouse said, "I know you want to catch me. But I can help you. I can find more toys and food for you." The cat was happy. The cat and the mouse became friends.
The cat learned that having a friend was better than catching the mouse. The cat and the mouse played together in the enormous house. They shared the toys and the food. The cat knew that having a friend was the best luxury of all. And they lived happily ever after.

Now tell me a story where a tough model falls down in a strong wind, surprising all the other toys who thought it was too strong to fall. The toys learn that it's okay to fall and that being there for each other is more important than being tough.

Once upon a time, there was a model. The model was very tough. The model liked to show off how strong it was. It would stand tall and not fall. All the other toys wanted to be like the tough model.
One day, a wind came and blew the model. The model did not want to fall. It tried very hard to stay up. But the wind was too strong, and the model fell. All the toys were surprised. They thought the model was too tough to fall.
After the fall, the model was not so tough anymore. The toys learned that it is okay to fall sometimes. They all helped the model to stand up again. And they all became friends. The toys learned that being tough is not the most important thing. The most important thing is to be there for each other and help each other when they fall.

You are a storyteller for young children.
Write a story that uses the words swing, blocks, and fancy.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Lily. She had lots of blocks to play with. She liked to stack them up high and then knock them down. One day, Lily went to the park with her mommy. There was a big swing there that she loved to go on. She swung back and forth and laughed and laughed. She felt like a bird flying in the sky. After playing on the swing, Lily went back home and built a fancy castle out of her blocks. It was the best day ever!
You are a storyteller for young children. In your stories, the characters talk to each other. Your stories have a problem that the characters must solve.

Can you tell me a story where a little girl named Isla goes to the beach with her family and becomes curious about the coal mine nearby. She asks a worker what they are doing and wants to help, but is told it's too dangerous. The worker promises to let her help number the coal next time?

Once upon a time there was a little girl named Isla. She was three years old and on a family outing to the beach. She was having lots of fun picking up shells and counting them as she went along. 
Isla heard a rumble coming from near the coal mine. She wanted to go and see what was happening. 
When Isla reached the edge of the coal mine she saw a large number of men loading big pieces of coal into a big truck. Isla was curious, so she asked one of the men what they were doing. He told her they were going to take the coal to the power plant. 
Isla asked if she could join them and the man said, "No, that's too dangerous for a little girl." 
Isla got angry. She stamped her foot and shouted, "It's not fair!" 
The man said, "I know it isn't, but that's the way it is. Coal is a disgusting, dirty thing and it's too dangerous for you to be near." 
Isla sulked and said, "But I just wanted to help number the coal!" 
The man smiled and said, "Well then, I guess the next time I come here we can number the coal together. But for now, it's time for you to go home and get some rest." 
And so Isla went home, happy
You are a storyteller for young children. In your stories, the characters talk to each other. Your stories have a sad ending.
Write a story that uses the words whistle, film, and smelly.

Once upon a time there was a little boy named Jack. Jack loved to whistle all day long. He had a friend named Charlie who loved films.
One day they decided to go to the cinema. When they got there, they heard an awful smell. Jack knew that smell! He said to Charlie,
